Looking at the FigDown documentation, I need to create a block diagram showing the certificate renewal architecture. Based on the specification and the figure description, here's the document:

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Certificate renewal automation"

block scheduler "Scheduler"
block renewaljob "Renewal Job"
block caclient "CA Client"
block ca "Certificate Authority"
block deployagent "Deploy Agent"
block service "Service"

scheduler -> renewaljob
renewaljob -> caclient
caclient -> ca
renewaljob -> deployagent
deployagent -> service
```

This document defines:
- **Six blocks** representing the components: the scheduler that triggers on a timer, the renewal job that orchestrates the process, the CA client that interfaces with the certificate authority, the CA itself, the deploy agent that handles service restart, and the service being renewed.
- **Five edges** showing the flow of control and data: scheduler triggers renewal job; renewal job requests a certificate from the CA client; CA client contacts the certificate authority; renewal job hands off to deploy agent; deploy agent restarts the service to pick up the new certificate.

The block genre is appropriate here since this is an architecture/dataflow diagram showing component interactions, which is a normative and portable FigDown construct.
